source.title_en: Berkshire Hathaway, Under a New CEO, Starts to Spend Its Cash Pile
source.title_zh: 新任 CEO 掌舵下，伯克希尔开始动用它的现金储备
source.author: Krystal Hur

overview_zh:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公布二季度财报：净利润翻倍至 256.7 亿美元，现金储备三年多来首次环比下降。公司斥资 68 亿美元收购住宅建筑商 Taylor Morrison Home，并买入 100 亿美元的 Alphabet 股票，同时回购自家股份。
这篇报道是典型的"财报快讯"体裁——结构固定、句式紧凑、专有名词密集。它的语言价值在于：一是财经高频词与固定搭配（回购、承保、未实现损益、环比下降），二是记者用来避免重复的替换表达（put a dent in、spending spree、put his stamp on）。学会这套词，你读任何一家公司的财报新闻都会轻松很多。

background.zh: 伯克希尔·哈撒韦，巴菲特创立的多元化控股集团，旗下有保险、铁路、能源、零售等业务
阿贝尔于今年 1 月接替巴菲特出任 CEO；巴菲特执掌该公司超过半个世纪
A 类股每股约 78 万美元，从不拆股；B 类股是为小投资者设立的低价股份
营业利润剔除投资损益，巴菲特认为它比净利润更能反映真实经营状况

vocab.en: a large corporation formed by merging separate and diverse firms
vocab.zh: （跨行业的）企业集团、综合性大企业
vocab.sentence: The Omaha, Neb.-based conglomerate said Saturday its quarterly profit more than doubled, powered by investment gains and strong results from its industrial and retail businesses.
vocab.note: 财经报道里，记者第二次提到某公司时几乎不会重复公司名，而是用一个概括性同位语替换：the conglomerate / the retailer / the chipmaker。读的时候要能立刻把它对应回前文的主语。

vocab.en: an amount acquired or accumulated, especially a large one
vocab.zh: （大笔的）所得、囤积量；此处 cash haul＝现金储备
vocab.sentence: Berkshire Hathaway put a dent in its massive cash haul during the second quarter.
vocab.note: haul 原指"拖、拽"，引申为"一次拖回来的东西"，因此自带"数量大、辛苦攒下"的意味，比中性的 amount 更有画面感。同义替换还有 cash pile、cash hoard、war chest。

vocab.en: to buy back one's own shares from the market
vocab.sentence: The company repurchased 478 Class A shares and more than 8 million Class B shares in May and June, for roughly $4.5 billion.
vocab.note: 口语和标题里更常用动词短语 buy back 和名词 buyback；正式财报文本用 repurchase。三者可互换，但 buyback 是名词、buy back 是动词短语，别写混。

vocab.en: compared with the immediately preceding period (quarter or month)
vocab.zh: 环比地（与上一季度／上月相比）
vocab.sentence: It marked the first time the company's cash declined sequentially in four years.
vocab.note: 财报里两个时间基准必须分清：sequentially＝环比（对比上一个季度），year over year / from a year earlier＝同比（对比去年同期）。本文两种都出现了，注意各自的参照物。

vocab.en: a burst of unrestrained activity, especially spending or buying
vocab.zh: 一阵狂热的行为；spending spree＝大举花钱、疯狂扫货
vocab.sentence: The spending spree is a sign that Greg Abel is beginning to put his stamp on the conglomerate.
vocab.note: spree 一定是短时间、高强度、略带失控意味的行为，所以既能说 shopping spree，也能说 killing spree。用在公司身上是轻微的调侃，暗示"花得比平时凶"。

vocab.en: the person who held a job or office before the current holder
vocab.sentence: Greg Abel is beginning to put his stamp on a conglomerate that his predecessor ran for more than half a century.
vocab.note: 成对记忆：predecessor（前任）↔ successor（继任者）；动词 succeed sb.＝接替某人（本文的 succeeded Warren Buffett），注意别理解成"成功"。

vocab.en: overflowing with excitement or enthusiasm; (of markets) buoyant and overheated
vocab.zh: （人）兴高采烈的；（市场）亢奋的、过热的
vocab.sentence: It's very hard to want Greg to be making big deals in an ebullient market like now.
vocab.note: 词源是"沸腾"（拉丁语 bullire＝to boil），所以形容市场时暗含"烧过头、迟早要冷"的贬义。市场情绪词的强度梯度：subdued < steady < buoyant < ebullient < frothy < bubble。

vocab.en: the insurance business of assessing risk and issuing policies (as distinct from investing the premiums)
vocab.zh: 承保（业务）；保险公司靠收保费、赔付理赔赚的那部分利润
vocab.sentence: The company's insurance arm reported a drop in underwriting earnings, weighed down by results from car insurer Geico.
vocab.note: 保险公司有两个利润来源，读财报必须分开：underwriting income（承保收益，保费减赔付）和 investment income（投资收益，用浮存金投资赚的）。本文说两者都下滑了。

vocab.en: (of a gain or loss) existing only on paper because the asset has not been sold
vocab.zh: 未实现的（浮盈／浮亏，尚未卖出兑现）
vocab.sentence: Accounting rules require Berkshire to include unrealized gains and losses from its giant investment portfolio when it reports net income.
vocab.note: realize 在财经语境里＝"变现、兑现"，不是"意识到"。realized gain 是卖出后落袋的收益，unrealized gain 只是账面浮盈，口语也叫 paper gains。

vocab.en: an irregular rise and fall in amount or value
vocab.sentence: Short-term fluctuations in the stock market can cause big swings in quarterly income.
vocab.note: 同一句里 fluctuations 和 swings 是刻意的同义替换（避免重复），这是英文写作的基本要求。近义强度：fluctuation（中性波动）< swing（大幅摆动）< volatility（波动性，可量化的术语）。

chunks.t: Berkshire Hathaway put a dent in its massive cash haul
during the second quarter,
repurchasing company shares and buying more stocks than it sold
for the first time in more than three years.

sentences.skeleton: Berkshire put a dent in its cash haul, repurchasing shares and buying more stocks than it sold.
sentences.zh: 伯克希尔在第二季度动用了它庞大的现金储备：回购了自家股票，并且三年多来首次买入的股票多于卖出的股票。

points.label: 现在分词作伴随状语
points.text: repurchasing... and buying... 不是并列谓语，而是分词短语，说明主句动作"put a dent in"是怎么发生的。这是新闻导语最常见的加信息方式：主句给结论，分词补细节，避免写成两个短句。

points.label: 比较结构省略
points.text: buying more stocks than it sold 完整形式是 than it sold stocks，than 引导的比较从句里重复成分被省略。这个说法等于 was a net buyer of stocks（净买入）。

points.label: put a dent in
points.text: 字面是"在……上砸出一个坑"，用来说"（终于）让一大笔钱／一个大数字有所减少"，比 reduced 生动得多，且暗示"减得不多，但方向变了"——正是本文的核心新闻点。

drill.prompt_zh: 用「主句 + 现在分词伴随状语」写一句：这家初创公司去年削减了开支，裁掉了两成员工并关闭了三个海外办公室。
drill.answer: The startup cut its costs last year, laying off a fifth of its staff and closing three overseas offices.

chunks.t: The spending spree is a sign
that Greg Abel,
who succeeded Warren Buffett as chief executive in January,
is beginning to put his stamp on a conglomerate
that his predecessor ran for more than half a century.

sentences.skeleton: The spending spree is a sign that Abel is beginning to put his stamp on a conglomerate.
sentences.zh: 这轮大手笔支出表明，今年 1 月接替巴菲特出任首席执行官的格雷格·阿贝尔，正开始在这家由其前任执掌了半个多世纪的集团上留下自己的印记。

points.label: 同位语从句 vs 定语从句
points.text: 第一个 that（a sign that...）是同位语从句，解释 sign 的具体内容，that 在从句里不作成分；最后一个 that（a conglomerate that his predecessor ran）是定语从句，that 作 ran 的宾语。两个 that 长得一样，功能完全不同——判断方法：去掉 that 后从句是否缺成分。

points.label: 主语被插入语切断
points.text: 主句从句的主语 Greg Abel 和谓语 is beginning 之间插了一整个非限制性定语从句（who... in January）。读到逗号要"挂起"主语，跳过插入部分先找谓语，再回头补信息。这是长句最常见的阅读陷阱。

points.label: put one's stamp on sth.
points.text: "给某事物打上自己的烙印"，指新领导者开始按自己的方式改造一个组织。近义：leave one's mark on、reshape sth. in one's own image。

drill.prompt_zh: 模仿这个结构（同位语从句 + 插入定语从句）写一句：股价下跌说明，去年才上市的这家公司正在失去投资者的信任。
drill.answer: The falling share price is a sign that the company, which went public only last year, is losing the trust of investors.

chunks.t: Accounting rules require Berkshire to include unrealized gains and losses
from its giant investment portfolio
when it reports net income,
meaning that short-term fluctuations in the stock market can cause big swings in quarterly income.

sentences.skeleton: Accounting rules require Berkshire to include unrealized gains and losses, meaning that fluctuations can cause big swings.
sentences.zh: 会计准则要求伯克希尔在报告净利润时，把其庞大投资组合的未实现损益也计算在内；这意味着股市的短期波动会造成季度利润的大幅起落。

points.label: meaning that... 结果状语
points.text: 分词短语 meaning that... 对整个主句作出解读，相当于 which means that... 或 and this means that...。财经和科技写作特别爱用它把"事实"和"事实的含义"接在一句里。可替换的同类表达：suggesting that、leaving sth. exposed、raising the risk that。

points.label: require sb. to do sth.
points.text: 注意 require 的宾语补足语用不定式（require Berkshire to include），而不是 require doing。类似结构：allow / enable / force / permit sb. to do。

points.label: 同义替换避免重复
points.text: fluctuations（波动）→ swings（起落），前后指的是同一类现象却换了词。写作时刻意做这种替换，是拉开水平差距最快的方式之一。

drill.prompt_zh: 用 meaning that 结构写一句：新规定要求平台披露算法细节，这意味着企业将更难以商业机密为由拒绝监管。
drill.answer: The new rules require platforms to disclose how their algorithms work, meaning that companies will find it harder to refuse scrutiny by citing trade secrets.

chunks.t: Profit
from Berkshire's portfolio of manufacturing, service and retailing businesses
—a group that includes industrial metal components, Duracell batteries and Flying J fuel stations—
jumped 24% to $4.47 billion.

sentences.zh: 来自伯克希尔制造、服务和零售业务组合的利润——这一板块包括工业金属部件、金霸王电池和 Flying J 加油站——大涨 24%，至 44.7 亿美元。

points.label: 主谓被破折号隔开
points.text: 主干只有 Profit jumped 24%，中间塞了一个介词短语加一个破折号同位语，主语和谓语相隔 20 多个词。破折号内的内容永远是可删的补充说明——先跳过读通主干，再回来看细节。

points.label: 涨跌幅的标准写法
points.text: jumped 24% to $4.47 billion＝"上涨 24%，至 44.7 亿"。介词分工固定：by＋变化幅度，to＋变化后的水平，from＋变化前的水平。动词强度梯度：edged up < rose < climbed < jumped < soared；下跌方向：edged down < fell < slid < slumped < plunged。

points.label: portfolio of...
points.text: portfolio 既指"投资组合"，也指"（企业的）业务组合、产品线"。本文是后者。

drill.prompt_zh: 用「主语 + 破折号同位语 + 谓语」写一句：该公司的海外收入——主要来自德国、日本和巴西——下滑了 12%，至 8.3 亿美元。
drill.answer: The company's overseas revenue—most of it from Germany, Japan and Brazil—fell 12% to $830 million.

chunks.t: Berkshire ended June with $364.7 billion in cash and Treasury bills
after accounting for a payable for purchasing some of the short-term government debt,
a 4% decrease from three months earlier.

sentences.skeleton: Berkshire ended June with $364.7 billion in cash and Treasury bills, a 4% decrease from three months earlier.
sentences.zh: 在扣除购买部分短期国债所产生的应付款项之后，伯克希尔 6 月末持有 3647 亿美元的现金及国库券，较三个月前下降 4%。

points.label: end + 时间 + with + 数字
points.text: end June with $X 是财报固定句式："截至 6 月末持有 X"。同类：closed the year with、entered the quarter with。

points.label: account for 的两个意思
points.text: 这里 after accounting for＝"在把……计算／扣除在内之后"。account for 另一个高频义是"占（比例）"：Exports account for 30% of revenue。第三个义是"解释"。三个意思全靠语境区分。

points.label: 名词短语作总结同位语
points.text: 句尾的 a 4% decrease from three months earlier 不修饰任何单个名词，而是概括前面整件事，相当于 which was a 4% decrease...。这种"逗号＋名词短语"收尾非常经济，值得主动模仿。

drill.prompt_zh: 用「逗号＋名词短语」总结收尾写一句：该行三季度末的坏账余额为 210 亿美元，较去年同期增长 18%。
drill.answer: The bank ended the third quarter with $21 billion in bad loans, an 18% increase from a year earlier.

chunks.t: The company's insurance arm reported a drop in underwriting earnings,
weighed down by results from car insurer Geico,
and investment income.

sentences.skeleton: The insurance arm reported a drop in underwriting earnings and investment income.
sentences.zh: 公司的保险板块报告称，承保利润和投资收益双双下滑，主要受车险公司 Geico 业绩拖累。

points.label: arm＝分部
points.text: arm 在公司报道里指"（大集团的）某一业务部门"：its insurance arm、the lending arm、the research arm。同义词：division、unit、segment。

points.label: 过去分词作后置修饰
points.text: weighed down by... 修饰前面的 a drop，说明下滑的原因。weigh down 字面"压得抬不起头"，是财经写作里表达"拖累"的最常用动词，通常用被动：earnings were weighed down by higher costs。

points.label: 阅读警示：并列成分被切断
points.text: 句尾的 and investment income 其实并列的是 underwriting earnings（即 a drop in A and B），中间插入的分词短语把它们分开了，很容易误读成"和投资收益"并列 Geico。遇到句末孤零零的 and + 名词，要往前找它真正的并列对象。

phrases.zh: 使（大数目）有所减少；削弱
phrases.note: 常搭配 savings / profits / lead：The repairs put a dent in our savings.

phrases.zh: 在某事物上留下个人印记
phrases.note: 多用于新上任的领导者按自己意图改造组织
财报报道表达"利润被某项业务拉低"的标准说法

phrases.zh: 增长一倍以上、翻了不止一番
phrases.note: 动词用法：profit more than doubled；反义是 more than halved

phrases.en: a net buyer / seller of sth.
phrases.note: 买入量减去卖出量后仍为正即 net buyer
放句尾表示"目前如此，但未必长久"，是记者留有余地的常用手法

phrases.en: as it turns out / it turns out that
phrases.note: 引出与预期不同的结论
The company is set to disclose more next week. 比 will 更书面
衔接相似的例子或观点
描述竞争对手互相跟进时的固定表达

quiz.q: Berkshire's cash declined ____ for the first time in four years, meaning it fell compared with the previous quarter.
quiz.explain: sequentially＝环比，参照上一个季度；year over year 是同比，参照去年同期。原文强调的是"三年多来第一次比上一季度少"，所以只能用 sequentially。

quiz.q: The new chief executive is beginning to put his ____ on the company his predecessor ran for decades.
quiz.explain: 固定搭配是 put one's stamp on sth.（留下个人印记）。leave one's mark on 也成立，但动词必须换成 leave；put one's mark 并非习惯说法。

quiz.q: Which pair correctly describes profits that exist only on paper because the shares have not been sold?
quiz.explain: unrealized gains＝未实现收益（浮盈），realize 在此意为"变现"而非"意识到"。underwriting income 是保险承保利润，operating earnings 是剔除投资损益的营业利润。

quiz.q: "The insurance arm's profit was ____ by weak results at Geico." Which choice fits the WSJ's usual wording?
quiz.explain: be weighed down by sth.＝被……拖累，是描述业绩被某项业务拉低的标准搭配。put a dent in 需要接宾语（put a dent in profits），语法上此处不通。

quiz.q: In "a sign that Greg Abel, who succeeded Buffett in January, is beginning to...", the clause "who succeeded Buffett in January" is:
options: a non-restrictive relative clause inserted between subject and verb
an appositive clause explaining the noun 'sign'
the main clause of the sentence
quiz.explain: who 引导非限制性定语从句，修饰 Greg Abel，被逗号隔开插在主语和谓语 is beginning 之间。解释 sign 内容的是前面的 that 从句（同位语从句），两者要分清。

quiz.q: "Profit jumped 24% ____ $4.47 billion." Which preposition is correct?
quiz.explain: 介词分工固定：by＋变化幅度（jumped by 24%），to＋变化后的水平（to $4.47 billion），from＋变化前的水平。此处 $4.47 billion 是涨完之后的数值，用 to。
